Define sentinel missing-value codes

Source: R/roles.R
sd_set_missing.Rd

Survey data often encodes missing responses with sentinel numeric or text codes (e.g. 99, -9, "En osaa sanoa") instead of a true missing value. sd_set_missing() records these codes in meta$missing_codes and replaces matching values with NA in the data itself, so that later pipeline steps (e.g. sd_summarise()) compute correct statistics.

Usage

sd_set_missing(x, codes, vars = NULL)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object.

codes

Either a vector of codes to apply to vars (e.g. c(99, -9)), or a named list mapping variable names to their own codes (e.g. list(tt1 = c(99, -9), avoin_palaute = "")) — in which case vars is ignored.

vars

Character vector of variable names to apply codes to. NULL (the default) applies to every variable in the data except those already known to have role "id" — see the warning above. Ignored when codes is a named list.

Value

The same sd_data object, with matching values in the data replaced by NA and meta$missing_codes updated.

Always name vars explicitly

Leaving vars as NULL applies codes to every variable in the data — including id, weight, and date columns. This is risky: an id variable coded 1:200 legitimately contains the value 99, and a blanket sd_set_missing(x, codes = 99) would silently turn that respondent's id into NA. In practice, always list the specific variables where the sentinel code is meaningful (typically your substantive survey items), e.g. vars = c("tt1", "tt2", "tt3") — never rely on the "apply to everything" default. If variable roles have already been set (see sd_detect_roles()), leaving vars as NULL at least skips variables with role "id" automatically and a warning is raised — but this is a safety net, not a substitute for naming vars.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Suositeltu: nimeä muuttujat aina eksplisiittisesti
aineisto <- sd_set_missing(aineisto, codes = c(99, -9),
                            vars = c("tt1", "tt2", "tt3"))

# Eri koodit eri muuttujille:
aineisto <- sd_set_missing(aineisto, codes = list(
  tt1 = c(99, -9),
  avoin_palaute = ""
))
} # }
